suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains no entire-agreement or supersession language stating that prior negotiations, representations, and communications on the same subject matter are replaced by this Agreement, leaving open disputes about which version of commitments governs between the parties. Additionally, the absence of an express carve-out preserving liability for fraud means that either party could invoke the integration clause to argue that fraudulent pre-contractual representations are merged out of existence and cannot ground a claim — a result that courts in many jurisdictions would resist but that creates unnecessary litigation exposure. Both omissions are market-standard elements of a properly drafted integration clause. No survival or cross-reference conflict is introduced by the proposed amendments.
suggestions.original_text: Integration; Precedence. Any Work Order or Change Order (as defined in Section 4.0 below) and other exhibits issued and executed pursuant to this Agreement will be made part hereof and incorporated herein by reference. To the extent any terms or provisions of a Work Order or Change Order conflict with the terms and provisions of this Agreement, the terms and provisions of this Agreement shall control, except to the extent that the applicable Work Order or Change Order expressly and specifically states an intent to supersede the Agreement on a specific matter.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Integration; Precedence. This Agreement, together with any Work Order or Change Order (as defined in Section 4.0 below) and other exhibits issued and executed pursuant to this Agreement, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to its subject matter, supersedes all prior agreements, negotiations, representations, and communications relating thereto, and will be made part hereof and incorporated herein by reference; provided, however, that nothing in this Section shall limit or exclude either party's liability for fraud. To the extent any terms or provisions of a Work Order or Change Order conflict with the terms and provisions of this Agreement, the terms and provisions of this Agreement shall control, except to the extent that the applicable Work Order or Change Order expressly and specifically states an intent to supersede the Agreement on a specific matter.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted imposes confidentiality obligations solely on Quintiles and its employees, with no reciprocal obligation protecting any confidential information that Quintiles may disclose to Sponsor in connection with the Services, creating a material bilateral imbalance. It also omits any standard of care governing how Confidential Information must be protected, which renders the obligation difficult to enforce and falls below market-standard practice. Additionally, there is no obligation to return or destroy Confidential Information upon expiration, termination, or the disclosing party's request, leaving sensitive information in the receiving party's possession indefinitely. These gaps could create enforceability risk and practical disputes regarding post-termination data handling.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, Quintiles and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to Sponsor. All such data and information (hereinafter “Sponsor Confidential Information”) written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to Quintiles and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and shall be considered the sole property of Sponsor.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, each party and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to the other party. All such data and information (hereinafter "Confidential Information") written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to the receiving party as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and the sole property of the disclosing party. Each party shall protect the other party's Confidential Information using no less than reasonable care. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement, or upon the disclosing party's written request, the receiving party shall promptly return or destroy all such Confidential Information of the disclosing party.

suggestions.reason: The need-to-know restriction as drafted confines disclosure to "the other party" but does not require that individual recipients within each organization—such as employees, contractors, or advisors—be themselves bound by confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those in this Agreement. Without that binding requirement, Confidential Information may flow to personnel who are not formally obligated to protect it, creating an enforcement gap that exposes both parties to unauthorized disclosure with no clear contractual remedy against those individuals. The parallel use restriction similarly limits use to "employees" only, which is narrower than the categories of personnel who may legitimately need access to perform obligations under the Agreement, creating a tension that could inadvertently put a party in breach through routine engagement of contractors or advisors.
suggestions.original_text: Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked ‘confidential’, or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information to the other party on a need-to-know basis and to the extent that Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party’s obligations hereunder. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period often (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked 'confidential', or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only disclose Confidential Information on a need-to-know basis to those of its employees, contractors, agents, and advisors who require access to such Confidential Information for its undertaking of this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth herein. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees, contractors, agents, and advisors only for purposes of performing the receiving party's obligations hereunder. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period of ten (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.

suggestions.reason: The clause defines Sponsor's Property and confirms its ownership, but leaves three commercially material gaps: it grants Quintiles no express licence to use Sponsor's Property, imposes no restriction limiting that use to the performance of this Agreement, and is silent on responsibility if either party's materials infringe a third party's intellectual property rights. Without a licence grant, Quintiles has no contractual authority to use Sponsor's materials even for contracted services, while the absence of a use restriction means there is no express bar on Quintiles using Sponsor's Property for unrelated purposes. The lack of any IP infringement responsibility exposes both parties to unallocated third-party claims arising from materials exchanged under the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor’s Property. Sponsor’s property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively “Sponsor’s Property”).
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor's Property. Sponsor's property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively "Sponsor's Property"). Sponsor hereby grants Quintiles a non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to use Sponsor's Property solely for the purpose of performing its obligations under this Agreement, and Quintiles shall use Sponsor's Property for no other purpose. Each party represents and warrants that the materials it supplies to the other party under this Agreement do not, to the best of its knowledge, infringe any third party's intellectual property rights.

suggestions.reason: The clause captures Quintiles' background IP—assets developed independently of this Agreement—but does not, within its own text, explicitly distinguish between pre-existing background IP and foreground IP created during performance of the Services. The cross-reference to Section 6.3a provides only an implicit carve-out for foreground IP, leaving parties without a clear, self-contained allocation rule in this clause, which creates interpretive risk and potential disputes over ownership of improvements or derivatives developed during engagement. Without an express statement that foreground IP is separately governed, a court or arbitrator could read the broad definition of "Quintiles' Property" as capturing IP developed during the Agreement if its nexus to Quintiles' business or operations is established. The fix requires only a targeted amendment to anchor the definition to pre-existing IP and add a single clarifying sentence directing foreground IP to Section 6.3a.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles’ Property. Any inventions, processes, know-how, trade secrets, improvements, other intellectual properties and other assets, including but not limited to analytical methods, procedures and techniques, procedure manuals, personnel data, financial information, computer technical expertise and software, which have been developed by Quintiles independent of this Agreement, which relates to Quintiles’ business or operations, and not falling within Section 6.3a below, shall remain the exclusive property of Quintiles (collectively “Quintiles’ Property”). For the avoidance of doubt, Quintiles’ Property shall not include any inventions, trade secrets or know-how that incorporates data, information or know-how derived from Sponsor’s Property of Sponsor Confidential Information.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles' Property. Any inventions, processes, know-how, trade secrets, improvements, other intellectual properties and other assets, including but not limited to analytical methods, procedures and techniques, procedure manuals, personnel data, financial information, computer technical expertise and software, which were owned by Quintiles prior to, or developed by Quintiles independently of, this Agreement, which relates to Quintiles' business or operations, and not falling within Section 6.3a below, shall remain the exclusive property of Quintiles (collectively "Quintiles' Property"). Any intellectual property first conceived or developed by Quintiles in the course of performing Services under this Agreement shall be allocated in accordance with Section 6.3a. For the avoidance of doubt, Quintiles' Property shall not include any inventions, trade secrets or know-how that incorporates data, information or know-how derived from Sponsor's Property or Sponsor Confidential Information.

suggestions.reason: The assignment of Project IP to Sponsor does not expressly carve out Quintiles' pre-existing proprietary technology (Quintiles' Property) from the scope of the assignment, meaning the broad operative language could be read to encumber IP that Quintiles owns independently and deploys across multiple client engagements — a risk the broader Agreement appears to address in a separate provision but which is absent from this operative paragraph. Additionally, the clause is entirely silent on responsibility for third-party claims alleging that Project IP, or the Services giving rise to it, infringe a third party's intellectual property rights, leaving both parties without any agreed allocation of that exposure. A targeted carve-out for Quintiles' Property within the assignment and a bilateral responsibility sentence for third-party infringement claims address both deficiencies without disturbing the core ownership structure.
suggestions.original_text: Any inventions and discoveries, including any data and information generated or derived by Quintiles as the result of Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement and/or uses Sponsor Confidential Information (collectively “Project IP”) are the sole and exclusive property of Sponsor and Quintiles hereby assigns to Sponsor any Quintiles rights to Project IP (including any patent and all other intellectual property rights therein). Project IP shall be deemed Sponsor Confidential Information for purposes of Section 5.1 above.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Any inventions and discoveries, including any data and information generated or derived by Quintiles as the result of Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement and/or uses Sponsor Confidential Information (collectively "Project IP"), excluding any Quintiles' Property or improvements thereto, are the sole and exclusive property of Sponsor and Quintiles hereby assigns to Sponsor any Quintiles rights to Project IP (including any patent and all other intellectual property rights therein). Each party shall be responsible for any third-party claims alleging that its own pre-existing intellectual property incorporated into the Project IP infringes such third party's intellectual property rights. Project IP shall be deemed Sponsor Confidential Information for purposes of Section 5.1 above.

suggestions.reason: The clause restricts Sponsor's use of the Quintiles Software to the specific project "in connection with" the Agreement, but it does not impose a symmetrical, express purpose limitation on either party's use of the other's intellectual property more broadly. As a result, Quintiles' use of Sponsor's Property in performing the Services and Sponsor's use of any licensed Quintiles IP are not expressly confined to the agreed contractual purpose, creating a gap that could permit use beyond what either party reasonably intends. This asymmetry is commercially unfair to both parties and, absent an explicit mutual purpose limitation, creates an enforceability risk where broader use could be argued as permitted by implication. The paragraph also contains a typographical error in the license grant ("with the right use by") that should be corrected to avoid ambiguity over the scope of the license.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor and Quintiles agree that any Quintiles’ Property or improvements thereto which are used, improved, modified or developed by Quintiles under the term of this Agreement, and which do not use or include any Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor’s Property, are the sole and exclusive property of Quintiles and shall be deemed Quintiles Confidential Information. To the extent the Quintiles Software (defined as programs for the purposes of data derivations, population identification, production of statistical analysis outputs, is determined to be necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement, Quintiles grants to Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license with the right use by only Sponsor (and not its Affiliates or other third parties) without the right to sell, assign or sublicense such software programs and any improvements thereto in connection with such Sponsor project under the Agreement. For such software, Quintiles will provide to Sponsor the macros. When Quintiles’ Software is no longer necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data as described above, such Quintiles Software shall be returned to Quintiles.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor and Quintiles agree that any Quintiles' Property or improvements thereto which are used, improved, modified or developed by Quintiles under the term of this Agreement, and which do not use or include any Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor's Property, are the sole and exclusive property of Quintiles and shall be deemed Quintiles Confidential Information. To the extent the Quintiles Software (defined as programs for the purposes of data derivations, population identification, production of statistical analysis outputs) is determined to be necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement, Quintiles grants to Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license with the right to use by only Sponsor (and not its Affiliates or other third parties) without the right to sell, assign or sublicense such software programs and any improvements thereto in connection with such Sponsor project under the Agreement. For such software, Quintiles will provide to Sponsor the macros. Each party shall use the other party's intellectual property solely for the purposes expressly authorized under this Agreement and for no other purpose. When Quintiles' Software is no longer necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data as described above, such Quintiles Software shall be returned to Quintiles.

suggestions.reason: The clause omits three market-standard compliance elements that create material legal and operational risk for both parties: it contains no anti-bribery or anti-corruption commitment, no supply-chain obligation addressing forced labour or human trafficking, and no mutual obligation to notify the other party upon becoming aware of a material regulatory breach affecting the Services. Additionally, Quintiles' standard operating procedures are referenced without any mechanism for Sponsor to access or verify them, and Sponsor's own compliance obligation is framed only as a passive cooperation undertaking rather than an affirmative commitment to comply with applicable laws in connection with its own responsibilities under the Agreement. These gaps could expose either party to regulatory and reputational liability that is entirely preventable with minimal additional language.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA’s electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 (“Part 11”), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles’ standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, and applicable laws prohibiting forced labour, child labour, and human trafficking within its supply chain, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA's electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 ("Part 11"), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles' standard operating procedures, copies of which shall be made available to Sponsor upon written request, will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Sponsor represents that it will comply with all applicable laws and regulations in connection with its own obligations hereunder and will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believe are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing upon becoming aware of any material breach of applicable law or regulation that affects the performance of the Services under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The termination-for-convenience right is granted solely to Sponsor, leaving Quintiles without a corresponding right to exit an unprofitable or operationally unworkable engagement, which creates an asymmetric commercial relationship that is not market-standard for a bilateral Master Services Agreement. Beyond the reciprocity gap, the clause is silent on survival of key provisions (such as confidentiality, payment, and intellectual property), transition assistance obligations and how they are charged, and any obligation on either party to cooperate with a replacement provider, all of which create material operational and financial uncertainty upon exit for both parties.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) day’s prior written notice to Quintiles.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party. Upon termination, Quintiles shall provide reasonable transition assistance at its then-current rates, and each party shall reasonably cooperate with any successor provider. Provisions that by their nature survive termination shall remain in effect.

suggestions.reason: The obligation for the parties to "promptly meet" to prepare a close-out schedule lacks a defined timeframe, leaving both parties exposed to uncertainty about when post-breach wind-down obligations are triggered and enforceable. Without a fixed period, either party could dispute whether the other acted with sufficient speed, potentially delaying orderly cessation of the Services and creating operational and financial risk for both sides. Additionally, the clause contemplates only a "close-out schedule" rather than a broader transition assistance obligation, which is insufficient for a services agreement where continuity of operations and knowledge transfer are commercially material at exit. These gaps may also interact with any survival or payment provisions governing the period between expiry of the cure period and final wind-down of the Services.
suggestions.original_text: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days’ written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days' written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then within five (5) Business Days thereafter the parties shall meet to prepare a close-out schedule that includes reasonable transition assistance for a period not to exceed thirty (30) days, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations.

suggestions.reason: The wind-down obligations imposed on Quintiles upon receipt of a termination notice are limited to financial reconciliation; the clause makes no provision for transition assistance such as the return of Client materials and data or a handover of work in progress, leaving the receiving party without enforceable entitlements that are standard in services agreements of this type. Without such obligations, a terminating party has no contractual basis to compel an orderly transition, which creates practical and operational risk for whichever party is relying on continuity of data or project records. The addition of a brief, defined transition assistance obligation closes this gap without materially altering the financial settlement mechanics already in place.
suggestions.original_text: Upon receipt of a termination notice, Quintiles shall promptly cease performing any work not necessary for the orderly close out of the affected Project(s), or for the fulfillment of any regulatory requirements, and will submit an itemized accounting of the Services completed, expenses incurred pursuant to the performance of the Services, any non-cancelable expenses incurred relating to the unfinished Work Order, and payments received in order to determine a balance to be paid by either party to the other. Such balance will be paid within thirty (30) days of receipt of such itemized accounting.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon receipt of a termination notice, Quintiles shall promptly cease performing any work not necessary for the orderly close out of the affected Project(s), or for the fulfillment of any regulatory requirements, and will submit an itemized accounting of the Services completed, expenses incurred pursuant to the performance of the Services, any non-cancelable expenses incurred relating to the unfinished Work Order, and payments received in order to determine a balance to be paid by either party to the other. Quintiles shall also provide reasonable transition assistance, including the return of Client materials and data and a summary handover of work in progress. Such balance will be paid within thirty (30) days of receipt of such itemized accounting.

suggestions.reason: The definition of "control" contains two related defects that undermine its enforceability. First, there is a typographical error — "polices" for "policies" — which, while facially minor, creates a latent ambiguity in a defined term relied upon throughout the affiliate and subcontracting framework. Second, and more materially, the alternative limb — "otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity" — introduces a subjective and undefined standard that could capture entities far beyond those contemplated by the 50% voting threshold, since minority shareholders or contractual counterparties might also "influence" a company's direction. This ambiguity could expose either party to disputes about whether a particular entity qualifies as an "affiliate" for purposes of Work Order execution, benefit entitlement, and obligations under this Agreement. Replacing the vague alternative limb with the market-standard "power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies" formulation removes the ambiguity and anchors the definition to an objectively assessable standard.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor’s affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor’s affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term “affiliate” shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term “control” shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity or otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles' obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor's affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor's affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term "affiliate" shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term "control" shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity or otherwise having the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of an entity, whether through ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise.

suggestions.reason: As drafted, Sponsor holds an unconstrained prior written approval right over every third-party subcontract without any corresponding obligation to act reasonably or within a defined period, creating a practical veto that could impede Quintiles' delivery of Services under any Project. While Quintiles is required to supply sufficient information to enable evaluation, Sponsor bears no corresponding duty to evaluate or respond within a reasonable time, leaving Quintiles exposed to indefinite delay. This imbalance is commercially unjustified given that Quintiles remains fully responsible for subcontractor performance under proviso (ii) and must impose equivalent contractual protections on subcontractors under proviso (iii). Adding a reasonableness qualifier to Sponsor's approval right corrects the asymmetry without undermining Sponsor's legitimate oversight interest.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles shall have the right to subcontract a portion of its obligations in connection with its performance of any Project (other than to its corporate affiliates), provided that (i) Quintiles shall have obtained the prior written approval of Sponsor to the subcontract, including providing Sponsor with sufficient information to enable proper evaluation of such subcontractor; (ii) such subcontract shall not relieve Quintiles of any of its obligations under this Agreement; (iii) Quintiles shall enter into a written agreement with each subcontractor on terms and conditions consistent with this Agreement, including for the benefit of Sponsor, provisions substantially similar to those of Sections 5.0,6.0, and 11.0; (iv) each Work Order, when appropriate, shall specify the name of such subcontractors; and (v) if requested by Sponsor, Quintiles agrees to provide Sponsor with a copy of each such subcontract.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles shall have the right to subcontract a portion of its obligations in connection with its performance of any Project (other than to its corporate affiliates), provided that (i) Quintiles shall have obtained the prior written approval of Sponsor to the subcontract, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, including providing Sponsor with sufficient information to enable proper evaluation of such subcontractor; (ii) such subcontract shall not relieve Quintiles of any of its obligations under this Agreement; (iii) Quintiles shall enter into a written agreement with each subcontractor on terms and conditions consistent with this Agreement, including for the benefit of Sponsor, provisions substantially similar to those of Sections 5.0, 6.0, and 11.0; (iv) each Work Order, when appropriate, shall specify the name of such subcontractors; and (v) if requested by Sponsor, Quintiles agrees to provide Sponsor with a copy of each such subcontract.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains two related imbalances. First, Sponsor's document-delivery obligation is anchored only to "a timely manner," a vague standard that creates enforceability uncertainty and provides no objective measure against which Sponsor's performance can be assessed. Second, and more significantly, the liability-exclusion sentence is entirely one-sided: Quintiles is fully insulated from consequences flowing from Sponsor's failure to cooperate, yet no reciprocal protection is afforded to Sponsor in the event Quintiles fails to perform or cooperate in a way that contributes to the same errors or delays. This asymmetry lacks commercial justification in a bilateral services arrangement where both parties bear cooperation obligations, and it may expose Sponsor to uncapped delay consequences even where causation is shared.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles in a timely manner all documents, materials and information in Sponsor’s possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Quintiles shall not be liable to Sponsor nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising from Sponsor’s failure to timely provide documents, materials or information or to otherwise cooperate with Quintiles in order for Quintiles to timely and properly perform its obligations under the relevant Work Order or Change Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles within the timeframes required to enable Quintiles to perform in accordance with the timelines set forth in the applicable Work Order or Change Order all documents, materials and information in Sponsor's possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Neither party shall be liable to the other nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences to the extent arising from the other party's failure to timely provide documents, materials or information or to otherwise cooperate as required under the relevant Work Order or Change Order.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "good faith efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution" combines two legally imprecise standards in a single operative obligation. "Good faith efforts" is not a recognized term of art under most governing law frameworks and lacks the objective content of "commercially reasonable efforts," making it difficult to assess compliance or establish breach. "Acceptable resolution" is equally open-ended, as it sets no measurable or objectively assessable benchmark against which either party's conduct or proposed remedy could be evaluated. Left unaddressed, these vague standards create a material risk that neither party can enforce the obligation, and any dispute over whether sufficient efforts were made would be resolved only by reference to extrinsic evidence.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles and Sponsor agree to notify the other in writing immediately if any delays or limits are encountered in their performance of any Work Order, and shall use good faith efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution to such delays or limits.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles and Sponsor agree to notify the other in writing immediately if any delays or limits are encountered in their performance of any Work Order, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to negotiate a mutually agreeable resolution to such delays or limits.

suggestions.reason: The "WORK ORDER" section contains no operative text addressing document hierarchy, leaving both parties exposed to conflicting obligations between this Agreement and any executed Work Orders with no mechanism to resolve them. Without a precedence rule, a Work Order could inadvertently override material Agreement terms—such as limitations of liability, confidentiality, or IP ownership—simply by restating or contradicting them, which creates material legal uncertainty and potential enforcement risk for both parties. Additionally, the absence of a provision excluding extraneous terms (such as pre-printed purchase order conditions or online platform terms) means that either party could argue that such terms are incorporated by reference, undermining the agreed commercial framework. These gaps are particularly significant in a Master Services Agreement structure, where consistent document hierarchy across multiple engagements is operationally essential.
suggestions.original_text: WORK ORDER
suggestions.suggested_fix:
WORK ORDER

Each Work Order is governed by and incorporated into this Agreement. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between a Work Order and this Agreement, the terms of this Agreement shall prevail to the extent of the conflict, unless the Work Order expressly states the specific provision of this Agreement it intends to modify and both parties execute the Work Order with that intent. No Work Order shall incorporate, attach, or give effect to any pre-printed, standard, or online terms of either party unless expressly agreed in writing by both parties.

suggestions.reason: The clause incorporates the Master Agreement by reference but fails to identify any schedules, exhibits, or attachments to this Work Order as documents forming part of the contractual arrangement, leaving the full scope of the documented agreement between the parties ambiguous. In practice, Work Orders under a Master Services Agreement are routinely accompanied by scopes of work, pricing schedules, or technical appendices that are essential to defining each party's obligations, and the omission of any reference to such documents creates an enforceability gap if a dispute arises over which materials govern. This ambiguity is a risk to both Sponsor and Quintiles, as neither party can point with certainty to a complete, closed set of documents constituting the Work Order.
suggestions.original_text: This Work Order (“Work Order”) is between ________ (“Sponsor”) and ________ (“Quintiles”) and relates to the Master Services Agreement dated ________, (the “Master Agreement”), which is incorporated by reference herein. Pursuant to the Master Agreement, Quintiles has agreed to perform certain services in accordance with written work orders, such as this one, entered into from time-to-time.
suggestions.suggested_fix: This Work Order ("Work Order"), together with any schedules and exhibits attached hereto, is between ________ ("Sponsor") and ________ ("Quintiles") and relates to the Master Services Agreement dated ________ (the "Master Agreement"), each of which is incorporated by reference herein and collectively constitutes the agreement of the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof. Pursuant to the Master Agreement, Quintiles has agreed to perform certain services in accordance with written work orders, such as this one, entered into from time-to-time.

suggestions.reason: The clause establishes that the Work Order is subject to the Master Agreement but fails to specify which document controls in the event of a conflict between their respective terms. Without an express order of precedence, any inconsistency between the Work Order and the Master Agreement creates genuine ambiguity that a court would need to resolve, exposing both parties to interpretive disputes over scope, fees, timelines, and other negotiated terms. Market-standard practice requires an explicit conflict resolution rule — typically that the Work Order prevails for subject-matter-specific terms while the Master Agreement governs for all other matters, or vice versa — so that neither party bears an unequal interpretive risk.
suggestions.original_text: Work Order. This document constitutes a “Work Order” under the Master Agreement and this Work Order and the services contemplated herein are subject to the terms and provisions of the Master Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Work Order. This document constitutes a "Work Order" under the Master Agreement and this Work Order and the services contemplated herein are subject to the terms and provisions of the Master Agreement. In the event of any conflict between this Work Order and the Master Agreement, the terms of this Work Order shall control solely with respect to the specific subject matter of this Work Order, and the Master Agreement shall control in all other respects.

suggestions.clause: Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses
suggestions.reason: The clause defers all fee and payment terms entirely to attachments without identifying, even at a high level, the basis on which fees are calculated. If an attachment is missing, incomplete, or disputed, neither party can establish from the body of the Work Order whether compensation is fixed, time-and-materials, or usage-based, creating a material enforceability gap. This ambiguity equally exposes the service provider to under-recovery and the recipient to open-ended or uncapped fee exposure. Because the fee methodology anchors downstream obligations such as invoicing, expense reimbursement, and any applicable caps, its absence from the operative text weakens the enforceability of those related provisions.

The specific services contemplated by this Work Order (the "Services") and the related payment terms and obligations, including the basis on which fees are calculated (whether fixed fee, time-and-materials, or usage-based), are set forth on the following attachments, which are incorporated herein by reference:

suggestions.clause: Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses
suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains no operative payment terms whatsoever, deferring entirely to attachments without establishing the core commercial mechanics that govern the financial relationship between the parties. As a result, neither party has enforceable protections regarding when invoices must be issued, when payment falls due, whether fees are fixed or subject to adjustment, how invoice disputes are handled, what consequences follow late payment, or how expenses are authorized and allocated. This creates material bilateral enforceability risk: the paying party has no basis to dispute an overcharge or challenge a fee variation, and the invoicing party has no remedy for delayed payment. The attachment-only structure also means that any amendment to an attachment could unilaterally alter fundamental payment obligations without the procedural safeguards ordinarily required by the body of the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6
suggestions.suggested_fix: SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6. Fees and expenses shall be as set forth in PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2, and are fixed unless amended in writing by both parties. The invoicing party shall issue invoices in accordance with PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4, and all undisputed amounts shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days following receipt of each invoice. Either party may dispute an invoice in good faith by providing written notice within ten (10) days of receipt; undisputed portions shall be paid by the original due date. Undisputed amounts not paid by the due date shall accrue interest at the lower of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law. Expenses, if any, are set out in PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2 and require prior written approval before being incurred by or charged to the other party.

suggestions.reason: The Term clause, as drafted, omits several operationally critical elements that expose both parties to material uncertainty: it does not specify what each Work Order must contain (such as scope, deliverables, timeline, or fees), does not require mutual execution to establish a binding Work Order, and provides no mechanism for changing the Work Order once executed. Without these guardrails, either party may dispute the agreed scope or pricing, unilaterally assert modifications, or challenge whether a Work Order was ever validly formed. The existing survival language linking the Work Order to the Master Agreement is partially adequate but does not address the hierarchy of terms in the event of a conflict between the two instruments, leaving that question unresolved.
suggestions.original_text: Term. The term of this Work Order shall commence on the date of execution and shall continue until the services described in Attachment 1 are completed, unless this Work Order is terminated in accordance with the Master Agreement. If the Master Agreement is terminated or expires, but this Work Order is not terminated or completed, then the terms of the Master Agreement shall continue to apply to this Work Order until the Work Order is either terminated or completed.

suggestions.reason: The clause permits Quintiles to use affiliates and lists pre-approved subcontractors but contains two material gaps that create bilateral risk. First, non-affiliate subcontractors and consultants are not expressly required to be bound by the same obligations—including confidentiality and data protection—as Quintiles itself, leaving Sponsor with no contractual privity or protection against those parties. Second, the clause provides no mechanism governing the engagement of additional or replacement subcontractors after execution, meaning Quintiles could substitute or add subcontractors without notice to or consent from Sponsor. Quintiles also bears no express primary liability for subcontractor performance, which creates an enforcement gap if a subcontractor causes harm.
suggestions.original_text: Affiliates and Subcontractors. Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Work Order. Any such affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of, and be entitled to all rights and protections afforded under, the Master Agreement and this Work Order. Any subcontractors or consultants (other than Quintiles’ affiliates) that will be used by Quintiles in performing the Services are listed below:

suggestions.reason: The provision, as drafted, is an unfilled placeholder that contains no operative language and, critically, no statement that Quintiles remains liable for the acts, omissions, or performance of any subcontractors or consultants it engages. Without a prime-contractor responsibility clause, the counterparty has no contractual assurance that Quintiles bears accountability for subcontractor failures, creating a material enforcement gap if a subcontractor causes delay, error, or harm. This omission also undermines any downstream remedy or indemnification mechanism elsewhere in the Agreement that may depend on Quintiles' responsibility for its extended workforce.
